questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed a field-free diode effect? The paper names devices #1, #2 and #3.
Why were any others set aside, and how was device #1 chosen for Figs. 1, 2 and 3(b)?
Which field, temperature and training ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown (sweeps between -50 and 50 mT at 200 mK, training at plus and minus 6 T)?
What does the second-best device look like? Could the field sweep of device #2 and the zero-field efficiency of device #3 appear in the main text, next to device #1?

Your p. 2 gives the trained field-free efficiency as "−71.4%", while the same paragraph, the abstract and Fig. 3(b) give 35.7% at 0 mT. Which value is right, and which sweep or state does each describe? Relatedly, what are |Ic+| and |Ic−| for device #3, so a reader can place the 705 µA excitation of Fig. 3(a) between them, given that Fig. 1(c) sweeps only to 300 µA in device #1?

How was zero applied field set and checked after the 6 T training and the 50 mT sweeps? Was the magnet's remanent field measured, for example with a Hall sensor, given that Meissner-screening diodes appear at fields near 1 Oe?

Does the trained diode state survive warming above the NbSe2 Tc, staying below the CrBr3 ordering temperature, and cooling back in zero field? That would separate trapped vortices from the CrBr3 magnetization.

Could you show the control in SM [40] in the main text: a bare NbSe2 flake or a NbSe2 region without CrBr3 from the same process and contact geometry, measured the same way? It sets the baseline from strain, edges and geometry, and helps explain the −15.2% after zero-field cooling.
